column1: # Renames for the Cadaver 2 disassembly - see renames/README.md.
# Most rows were produced by `tools/renames.py port` from the Cadaver 1 table (matching by instruction-aware signature or string content);

column9: comment

INT 9 handler (IVT[9] = 1000:11E9 in the running game). Reads port 60h, tracks Ctrl (1Dh/9Dh), records Ctrl+C (2Eh) / Ctrl+Q (10h) in abort_scancode, stores the last make code in last_scancode, looks the scancode up in key_bit_table to set/clear bits in input_held_bits/input_pressed_bits, then chains to old_int9_vector. [ported from cadaver1/cad 0x111e9 by sig16 match]
Saves the INT 8 vector to cs:148C, programs PIT channel 0 with divisor 5CECh (~50.2 Hz) and hooks INT 8 with timer_isr (1000:14E5). [ported from cadaver1/cad 0x1149c by sig16 match]
Restores the saved INT 8 vector and resets PIT channel 0 to divisor 0 (18.2 Hz). [ported from cadaver1/cad 0x114c8 by sig16 match]
INT 8 handler: calls the optional far callback timer_callback (music tick), bumps timer_ticks and the game clock bytes at 1F722..1F728. [ported from cadaver1/cad 0x114e5 by sig16 match]

Collision test for a box. In: dl,dh = x1,y1, ch = z of the mover (z-bottom), es:di = the mover's sprite block header (box sizes at +10h,+12h,+14h), si = its position record. Out: list of overlapped objects (position record pointers) at ds:[3Ch] (count in its first byte; first+1 = FDh when a solid object or the room boundary is hit; FFh = blocked by a door rectangle), ZF = no overlap. Checks z<0, z+h>=F0, x1>=ds:5F4, y1>=ds:5F5, the wall corner (x0<=ds:5DF and y0<=ds:5E0), x0<ds:5D2, y0<ds:5D1, the door rectangles ds:5E4.., then every object entry (x/y/z interval overlap, all inclusive). An entry is solid when entry[14h] is negative (FFh by default, set to the entry number for objects whose sprite header flag (byte 0Ch) bit 0 is set, i.e. flat floor things). [ported from cadaver1/cad 0x116e0 by sig16 match]
ds:5F4 / ds:5F5 = room width / height * 8 (record bytes +4/+5): the first x1/y1 outside the floor, used by collision_test. [ported from cadaver1/cad 0x11a29 by sig16 match]

Expands the current room's wall record (MP1 section 1) into the grid buffer at es:09C2 (2-byte cell stride, 16 bytes per row): byte 0 = slots per column, then the right-wall columns (thing[+4] = room width) and the left-wall columns (thing[+5] = room height), each a bottom-to-top stack of wall tile ids. Layout verified by reconstructing the whole room shell (tools/roomview.py render_shell).

For every object entry (50 bytes at ds:2A, count ds:224) whose sprite block header has the 'animated' bit (byte +0Ch & 4) and whose position record is not hidden: calls anim_step_object (sub_13BC5) and stores the new frame pointer ([si+1Eh]) / segment ([si+2Ah]) in the entry. Called once per game-loop step (every 2 timer ticks). [ported from cadaver1/cad 0x13b35 by sig16 match]

One step of an object's sprite animation. State = 10 bytes at [position record + record[0Eh]]: delay, frame, direction, script position, frame dx/dy words, cadence counter and reload. Runs the script words stored after the block header (low byte of the word pair = frame, the other byte = command 0xF3..0xFF dispatched through anim_command_table). Reimplemented in tools/animation.py and src/engine/anim.c, compared on all animated blocks and against a trace of the running game (flame bowl). [ported from cadaver1/cad 0x13bc5 by sig16 match]

Room entry, wall part: expands the wall record (room_expand_wall_columns), clears the 4 door rectangles at ds:5E4..5F3 (FFFF = none), sets ds:5D1/5D2 = room record bytes +14h/+15h (wall thickness in 1/8 cells: x0 >= 5D2 and y0 >= 5D1 for a walkable box), and ds:5DF / ds:5E0 = 2 + 8*(columns with a right wall) / 10 + 8*(columns with a left wall) (the L-shaped corner region where a box is blocked). [ported from cadaver1/cad 0x14714 by sig16 match]

Builds the 50-byte object entries from the room list (1000:4A00..4C50, layout in docs/formats.md 6.12), then room_setup_walls and the exit list (1000:4CFA..4ECD, reproduced in tools/roomexits.py). [ported from cadaver1/cad 0x14a00 by sig16 match]

Builds the exit entries (ss:[3A] list, count ds:22E) of the current room from the door ids in the room record and MP2 section 1 (door positions) - see tools/roomexits.py / docs/formats.md 6.12. Reproduced exactly for all 72 rooms of level 1. [ported from cadaver1/cad 0x14cfa by sig16 match]

Projects one object (ds:si = 50-byte object entry) to the screen. [si+0Ah] points to its 16-byte position record (x, y, z bytes in 1/8-cell units; x>>3, y>>3 = cell, x&7, y&7 = sub-cell), [si+6]:[si+8] to its sprite block header. Cell video offset from the table at ds:08DC (built by room_setup_floor_origin), sub-cell offset+shift from the 64-entry table at ds:F8CE, then subtracts (z - hdr[+2] + hdr[+10h] + hdr[+12h] + hdr[+14h]) rows and (hdr[+4]-1) words. Writes screen offset to [si+0Ch], y to [si+10h], pixel shift to [si+11h]. Found by hooking writes to those fields. [ported from cadaver1/cad 0x15a61 by sig16 match]

Moves the player and everything attached to it (list at ds:80h, count ds:602) by (dl, dh, ch) = (dx, dy, dz) in 1/8 cells: adds the deltas to each entry's box (+0..+5) and position record, then re-projects (sub_1530E). [ported from cadaver1/cad 0x167df by sig16 match]

dx = string index. bp = text_strings_ptr + table[text_offsets_ptr + 2*dx] (both ss-relative), stores dx in ds:023C, then text6_decode. The table is the .LNG offset table converted to little endian; the string area is the .LNG string area minus its first two bytes. [ported from cadaver1/cad 0x175af by sig16 match]

Decodes a packed string at ds:bp into ds:0A62 (es:[784h] segment): 6-bit codes, 4 per 3 bytes MSB first, translated through text6_alphabet (code 0 terminates, FFh entries are skipped). [ported from cadaver1/cad 0x175ca by sig16 match]
xlatb through bx=text6_alphabet-1; stores the char unless it is FFh; returns ZF set for code 0. [ported from cadaver1/cad 0x1762b by sig16 match]

dx = sprite number, ds:bx = object, es:di = destination. Reads the PCMAN sprite directory at A000:A000 (VRAM plane 2, or plane 3 when the directory word's high byte is >= 6, read map select 2/3), copies hot_x/hot_y into object+4/+6 and then rep movsw's the w,h header plus bitmap into RAM. Traced in tools/dosemu (reads at 1000:8E1A come from VRAM offsets A000h+(dir+6)*16). Record format: tools/pcman.py. [ported from cadaver1/cad 0x18d86 by sig16 match]

Entry of the masked sprite drawer: ax = x pixel, dx = y (row index into vram_row_offsets), cl = blit mode (1..), es:si = sprite data in RAM (mask plane, then 4 colour planes, per-plane stride ss:3B16). Computes di = row offset + x/8 and the shift x&7, then jumps through sprite_blit_mode_table. [ported from cadaver1/cad 0x18e26 by sig16 match]

column9: Jumps to the blit variant selected by dl through sprite_blit_mode_table (cs:8E5B + 2*dl). [ported from cadaver1/cad 0x18e71 by sig16 match]

column9: Opens the config file named at ss:4C73 (cadaver.ini) and reads 200 bytes to ds:07B0; parses sound/video/input choices. Traced in tools/dosemu: READ CADAVER.INI 1f17:07b0 200. [ported from cadaver1/cad 0x1b2c6 by sig16 match]

Counterpart of Cadaver 1's open_data_file (same register save/restore, '?' -> disk digit, 4-byte mjm header read to cs:D03A-4); extended - it also tests the digit against 54h ('T') - [matched by structure, not signature].
Counterpart of Cadaver 1's mjm_read. Adds a branch for method word cs:D03A == 326Dh ('m','2' = RNC, at loc_1CF65) before the 316Dh ('m','1' = DCL) test; [matched by structure, not signature].
explode output callback (second argument pushed by mjm_read): copies decompressed bytes to the caller's buffer and resumes the caller. [ported from cadaver1/cad 0x1c8fb by sig16 match]
explode input callback (first argument pushed by mjm_read): DOS read of *size bytes from handle word_1F8EE. [ported from cadaver1/cad 0x1c934 by sig16 match]

Draws the isometric floor of the current room: ds:[5E] = room record (+4 width, +5 height in cells), ds:[38] = floor map (tile id bytes, 0 = no tile, one padding column/row), tile bitmap = ds:[10] + id*168h (360 bytes: mask + 4 colour planes of 32x18, segment ds:[0E]). Cell (col,row) goes to di + col*142h + row*13Eh (+16 px/+8 lines per column, -16 px/+8 lines per row). Each tile is queued as a 16-byte draw entry (ds:[34]) and drawn with the OR blit sub_19080. Output matches the running game (tools/roomview.py). [ported from cadaver1/cad 0x1d1fa by sig16 match]

Looks up the video offset of floor tile (0,0) for the current room's size in floor_origin_table[(h-3)*8 + (w-3)] (h, w = bytes +5, +4 of the room record at ds:[5E]), stores it in ds:[58] and builds the per-column offset list at ds:08DC (+142h per column, +13Eh per row). A 10x10 room starts at pixel (144, 29): verified by pixel comparison with the running game. [ported from cadaver1/cad 0x1d2c5 by sig16 match]

column8: 33 FF B9 A0 0F EB 00 BA C4 03 B8 02 0F EF BA CE
column9: Clears one 8000-byte plane page: map mask 0Fh, write mode 0, then rep stosw of zero (cx=0FA0h) to the segment at ds:0002. Traced: the rep stosw at 1000:D4C3 wrote zeros to VRAM pages 0000h/2000h/4000h. [ported from cadaver1/cad 0x1d4a0 by sig16 match]

For video type 'C' (ds:07AB == 43h, colour VGA): converts the 16 big-endian Atari-ST palette words at ds:si into 6-bit DAC triples (0FF0Fh..) and programs them with INT 10h AX=1002h (EGA palette registers) and AX=1012h (48 DAC registers). [ported from cadaver1/cad 0x1d4c6 by sig16 match]
Copies 1F40h (8000) bytes = one EGA plane page from the segment at ds:0 to the segment at ds:2 with the VGA latches (write mode 1). [ported from cadaver1/cad 0x1d7cc by sig16 match]

column8: BA C4 03 B8 02 0F EF BA CE 03 B8 05 01 EF B8 07
column9: Programs the VGA: sequencer map mask 0Fh, GC mode 1 (write mode 1), colour-don't-care 0, no rotate/function; used before latch copies. [ported from cadaver1/cad 0x1d7e7 by sig24 match]

Loads and enters room ds:232h: fetches the player/room records (sub_1410E), sets ds:5Ch (player position record) / ds:5Eh (room record), calls room_set_bounds, floor origin setup, then sub_14A00 (build objects, walls, exits). Can be called directly in the emulator for any valid room number (tools/emu_call.py) - used as ground truth for exits and wall limits of all 72 rooms of level 1. [ported from cadaver1/cad 0x1da60 by sig16 match]
Drains the BIOS keyboard buffer (INT 16h peek + read until empty). [ported from cadaver1/cad 0x1dec8 by sig16 match]
Blocks (INT 28h idle) until a key is available and reads it, skipping extended-key prefix bytes. [ported from cadaver1/cad 0x1dee4 by sig16 match]

PKWARE DCL explode: reads 2 KiB chunks via read callback, validates header (type 0/1, dictionary bits 4..6), builds Huffman tables, decodes. Error codes 1..4 returned in AX. [ported from cadaver1/cad 0x1ec7a by sig16 match]
far entry: pushes 1DFD:0CAA (dcl_explode) and calls sub_1E052. [ported from cadaver1/cad 0x1ecd3 by sig16-near match]
Inner decode loop of the explode; returns 306h at end of stream. [ported from cadaver1/cad 0x1edcd by sig16 match]
PRESS KEY / 1 ENGLISH / 2 FRANCAIS / 3 DEUTSCH prompt text. [ported from cadaver1/cad 0x2e956 by content match]

Code->char table for text6_decode, 1-based (the byte before it, 0, is the terminator): A-Z, space . , 0-9, CR CR - ? " < = > (< = > stand for national letters, e.g. O/U umlaut), then 16 x FFh for codes 48..63. [ported from cadaver1/cad 0x2e9c3 by content match]
'DAC 1 HEAP TO BIG BY 0000 BYTES' error text (preceded by the 4 bytes 'mjm0'); the digits are patched in at run time. [ported from cadaver1/cad 0x2ea02 by content match]
Default saved-game path data\mike_save. [ported from cadaver1/cad 0x2ea2f by content match]

The game's 16-colour palette as 16 little-endian Atari-ST words (0RGB, 3 bits per channel); the same 16 words (big endian) sit in every level's LEVn.MP1. [ported from cadaver1/cad 0x2ea32 by content match]

ds:F8CE (initialised data in CAD.EXE, file offset 0x1EAEE): 64 entries (word video offset, word pixel shift) indexed (y&7)*8+(x&7) = screen displacement of an object sub-cell (1/8 cell units) from its cell origin. Irregular, not a formula (e.g. (7,1)=9 rows, (6,3)=11 rows); used by object_project. As pixels (offset*8+shift) the table is in tools/objplace.py SUB.
